question: Does updating an existing Cirrove DesktopVault item with a distinct 11,645-byte poorly compressible value reproduce the real iCloud reauthentication loss after desktop keyring persistence?
arms: create unique synthetic item with deterministic value A and verify
update the same item with distinct deterministic value B and verify immediately from a fresh process
verify B again at least 90 seconds later, recording whether the keyring file changed
endpoint: Record exact value equality and keyring file modification time only; never print either synthetic value or read a real credential. One run identifies a direction, not a failure rate.
prediction: If the failure lies in persisting an update to an existing Secret Service item, B may become empty after the keyring file is next written. If B survives, that update path alone is insufficient to reproduce the real-session loss.

environment.restriction: No compilation during the control window; no daemon restart; clear the exact synthetic key on completion.

interpretation: The synthetic existing-item update remained readable for about four minutes, but the keyring file was not written between the update and delayed check. This arm cannot decide whether a later file write would retain the updated value. The real iCloud item became empty in the same interval as a keyring-file write.
